source.citation: Kushch, Volodymyr I. (2020). Numerical algorithm of multipole expansion method for conductivity of ellipsoidal particle composite. Preprint, April 2020, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/340627510.

transcription.from: the preprint (PDF), read on the page text
transcription.note: Ellipsoid of semi-axes (1.5, 1.0, 0.5). Table 1: normalization constants gamma of surface harmonics at the finest quadrature printed (NC = 20), with the scale factors of the header (10^2, 10^5) applied; the labels of the harmonics within a degree are not used, the tests finding each value among the 2n + 1 constants of its degree. Table 2: Maxwell estimate of lambda11 at the fraction 0.5 with a Kapitza interface of conductance hc; the conductivity ratio is not restated for this table, and the values are recovered with lambda1/lambda0 = 100 (the residual example just before it uses 10). Table 3: coefficients eta of the translation of an exterior harmonic on the interior ones of a second ellipsoid at alpha e3, by projection on its surface (Eq. (33)); eta_nmkl is the coefficient of the interior harmonic (n, m) of the receiver for the exterior harmonic (k, l) of the sender.

semi_axes.description: Semi-axes of the ellipsoids of Tables 1 to 3.

fraction.description: Volume fraction of the Maxwell estimate of Table 2.

contrast.description: Conductivity ratio with which Table 2 is recovered, the table not restating it.

notes: Table normalization: Table 1, p. 8, last quadrature row, by degree n.
Table maxwell_kapitza: Table 2, p. 10, the columns being the conductance hc of the Kapitza interface.
Table translation: Table 3, p. 15, column Eq. (33) (direct integration), with nmax = 15.
